headline: 6 million Bangladeshi CVs for sale on dark web, hackers claim
summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen data from recruitment platform Bdjobs, offering the dataset for $1,000 to a limited number of buyers.
details: A hacker group calling itself 'madarax' has advertised the CVs of six million Bangladeshi jobseekers for sale on a dark web forum.
The group claims the data was sourced from the recruitment platform Bdjobs and includes names, phone numbers, addresses, emails, educational qualifications, and employment histories.
The dataset is being offered for $1,000, with the hackers stating it will be sold to a maximum of five buyers via payment methods like Binance and Wise.
Bdjobs has rejected these claims, stating that misleading and false information regarding the security of its website is being circulated on social media.
The company emphasized that it has prioritized user data protection since its founding and maintains strict security measures and access controls.
Bdjobs noted that while registered employers can access jobseeker information for recruitment, the company will take legal action if any employer sells that data to third parties.

headline_marked: Kurigram: [[Farmers break into warehouse]], take 197 sacks of urea
headline: Kurigram: Farmers break into warehouse, take 197 sacks of urea
summary: Agitated farmers in Bhurungamari upazila took the fertiliser amid a severe supply shortage for Aman rice cultivation.
details: Angry farmers in Kurigram’s Bhurungamari upazila broke into a dealer’s warehouse and took away 197 sacks of urea fertiliser today.
The incident occurred around 11:00 am at the dealer point of Messrs Shah Amanat Traders in Shilkhuri union, where over 200 farmers had gathered since morning.
Tensions rose after the dealer point remained closed for a long time, leaving farmers uncertain about obtaining the necessary fertiliser for Aman rice cultivation.
Local residents alleged that the dealer, Taifur Rahman Mukul, failed to distribute fertiliser on time despite receiving adequate allocations.
According to the OC of Bhurungamari Police Station, the demand for fertiliser in the union was 4,000 sacks, but only 1,320 sacks were allocated.
Police intervened to bring the situation under control, and through their efforts, 33 of the 197 sacks were later returned.
The dealer claimed that a group of miscreants joined the farmers to loot the warehouse and that the government allocation was simply lower than the actual demand.
